sections.changelog:
<pre># Changelog
All notable changes to "XO Functions" will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).

## [2.11.0]
### Fixed
- **Plugin Update Checker never delivered an update to any fleet site.** Root cause confirmed
  2026-09-26: `xo-functions.php` §6 pointed PUC at `https://github.com/wadellc/xo-functions`, but
  that source repo is private — every site's unauthenticated GitHub API check against it returns
  404, so PUC had nothing to compare against since the very first release (the 2026-09-20 tagging
  fix was necessary but never sufficient). See ROADMAP.md's "ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED" entry for the
  full investigation and the options considered. Updates now come from a public PUC "custom JSON"
  metadata channel (`XO_UPDATE_METADATA_URL`, overridable per site in `wp-config.php`) published by
  CI to the public, releases-only `wadellc/xo-functions-releases` repo on every version bump — the
  source repo itself stays private. **Because no site can self-update to the release that fixes
  self-updating, every site needs one manual update to 2.11.0.**

## [2.10.0]
### Added
- **`[copyright]` shortcode** (`wp-frontend/shortcodes.php`) — outputs "© {year} {site name}" using
  the site's own `get_bloginfo( 'name' )` by default (overridable via a `name` attribute). Added
  while auditing Lakemoor HOA's live, pre-consolidation `Exo-Functions` fork (see ROADMAP.md's
  fleet-audit entry): its equivalent shortcode had the organization name hardcoded to a
  *different* client entirely — a copy-paste mistake sitting live on Lakemoor's site. A generic,
  per-site-aware shortcode here structurally prevents that exact mistake from recurring, same
  reasoning as `search-url-slug.php`'s fix of a similarly copy-pasted bug.

## [2.9.0]
### Added
- **New `notifications` module — fleet alert-email noise control.** David's inbox: 756 threads
  sitting unread, 201 in the last 14 days, only 3 of the last 50 from an actual human — everything
  else machine-generated (WP auto-update notices, Wordfence digests, Search Console/Analytics
  reports). Real signal was getting buried: Wagner's Golf Shop's WooCommerce PayPal Payments
  plugin failed to auto-update on production for days, its failure notice arriving twice daily
  into a wall of identical-looking mail, unread. New `extend/notifications/` module, dedicated
  rather than folded into `wp-core`, since this is a fleet-wide alerting-behavior change, not an
  admin convenience — gets its own toggle surface and room to grow (Wordfence enforcement, MainWP
  wiring) without burying that inside an existing module. Four independently-toggleable filters,
  each suppressing exactly one WP core notification hook — deliberately never a blanket `wp_mail()`
  kill switch, so client-facing mail (Gravity Forms notifications, WooCommerce order/shipping mail,
  genuine user-facing password resets) can never be caught by this: `suppress-auto-update-emails`
  (bundles `auto_core_update_send_email`/`auto_plugin_update_send_email`/`auto_theme_update_send_email`
  — one behavior, one toggle), `suppress-password-change-email` (`send_password_change_email`),
  `suppress-new-user-admin-email` (`wp_new_user_notification_email_admin`, admin copy only), and
  `suppress-debug-update-email` (`automatic_updates_send_debug_email`).
  **Every toggle here defaults OFF, even on a brand-new install** — the one exception to this
  plugin's usual "new features default on" pattern (see `xo_get_default_feature_toggles()`).
  Suppressing update-failure mail without a replacement signal is exactly how the Wagner's failure
  went unnoticed in the first place; MainWP's own update-status/scan digest reporting is the
  intended replacement channel, and enabling this per site before that coverage is confirmed would
  recreate the same blind spot. See ROADMAP.md for the still-open follow-up work (MainWP digest
  setup, Wordfence option enforcement, fleet-visibility gap) this module deliberately doesn't
  attempt to solve on its own.

## [2.8.0]
### Added
- **Settings Import/Export** (new "Import / Export" tab, Settings > XO Functions) — David, 2026-08-29: wanted a way to make migrating XO Functions' configuration to production simpler, rather than re-clicking every toggle by hand. Export downloads a JSON file of this site's module toggles, granular feature toggles, Content Ordering's enabled post types/taxonomies, and Maintenance Mode's bypass roles; Import re-applies a previously exported file, running every value back through the exact same sanitize callback its own settings form already uses, so nothing an uploaded file contains can bypass normal validation. Deliberately never imports Maintenance Mode's on/off state or its selected Page ID — a Page ID from another site's database has no reliable meaning here, and silently importing "Maintenance Mode: ON" onto a live site could take it down unexpectedly; both stay something an admin sets manually per site. Single new registry (`xo_get_exportable_settings_keys()` in `xo-wp-settings.php`) drives both directions, so a future portable setting only needs to be added there once.

## [2.7.0]
### Added
- **Granular per-file feature toggles**, on top of the existing per-module toggles. `xo_get_feature_registry()` (xo-functions.php) is now the single source of truth listing every individually-toggleable file per module; each module's `index.php` loader gates its `require_once` calls on `xo_feature_enabled( $module, $feature )`, and the Modules settings tab renders a nested checkbox list per module straight from the same registry. Stored in a new `xo_functions_feature_toggles` option (multisite-scoped the same way as the existing module option). Defaults to "everything on" until a site's admin actually saves the settings form, so upgrading doesn't silently disable anything already running. `ordering-settings.php` + `post-type-ordering.php` + `taxonomy-ordering.php` are bundled under one `content-ordering` toggle rather than three independent ones — the latter two reference constants the first defines, so a partial toggle would fatal.
- **Pages List: "Last Updated" column** (`wp-core/pages-last-updated-column.php`) — sortable column on wp-admin's Pages list showing each page's last-modified date/time; core only shows the original Published date there. Sorting maps directly to `WP_Query`'s native `modified` orderby key, no custom query handling needed.
- **Plugins List: "Activation Date" column** (`wp-core/plugins-activation-column.php`) — starts recording each plugin's most recent activation time (via the `activated_plugin` action) and shows it as its own column on wp-admin/plugins.php. A plugin already active before this shipped has no historical timestamp and shows "Not tracked." Cleans up a plugin's stored timestamp when it's deleted (`deleted_plugin` action), so the option doesn't accumulate stale entries.
- **Plugins List: default to "Active" view** (`wp-core/plugins-default-active-view.php`) — wp-admin/plugins.php now lands on the Active filter instead of All, matching the same default-to-active pattern already used for the Gravity Forms form list. Only fires when no `plugin_status` (or search) is present, so it never overrides an explicit view.
## [2.6.1]
### Fixed
- **Cart icon leak persisted after 2.6.0's wp_head()/wp_footer() removal** — caught via direct HTML inspection immediately after deploying 2.6.0 to prod, before it could be mistaken for fixed: the site's side-cart plugin doesn't hook `wp_head`/`wp_footer` for this at all — it hooks `the_content` filter itself to append its floating cart button's markup (and enqueue its own CSS/JS) to every page's rendered content, which this function still has to call to render the maintenance page's own blocks. Switched from the full `apply_filters( 'the_content', ... )` chain to calling `do_blocks()` directly — the specific WordPress core function that actually renders block markup, normally just one of many callbacks hooked to `the_content` alongside whatever a theme or plugin has also hooked there. Renders exactly this page's own blocks, nothing a third party has additionally hooked onto `the_content`. Trade-off: `wpautop`/`wptexturize`/`do_shortcode` (also normally on `the_content`) don't run either — acceptable for a page meant to stay plain and block-built.
- Confirmed via direct HTML inspection on prod (not just visual review) that Astra's heading style is genuinely unaffected — the only `text-transform` present is WordPress core's own harmless button-reset rule (`text-transform: inherit`).
- Noted, not yet fixed: Astra defines its content-width through its own indirection (`--wp--style--global--content-size: var(--wp--custom--ast-content-width-size)`), and that inner custom property isn't defined anywhere in this page's output — so the Group block's width constraint likely still won't apply specifically on Astra/prod, unlike on stage's ona-pro. Lower severity than the cart/heading leaks (cosmetic width only, not interactive or theme-quirk bleed-through); worth a follow-up.

## [2.6.0]
### Fixed
- **Maintenance page leaked plugin UI and theme styling it shouldn't have** — confirmed live on Wagner's prod (Astra + WooCommerce): a fully interactive floating cart button (the site's own side-cart plugin, hooked to `wp_footer`) appeared on the maintenance page, and the active theme's own global heading style (uppercase transform) overrode how the content was authored to look. Root cause: calling `wp_head()`/`wp_footer()` fires every plugin's own hooked output indiscriminately, and pulls in the theme's own stylesheet. Both calls removed entirely.
- **Removing those two calls broke correct block rendering in several distinct ways, each root-caused and fixed in turn:**
  - Since WordPress 5.9, each core block registers its own separate stylesheet handle, only enqueued as a side effect of actually rendering the block (during `the_content`) — printing styles in `<head>` before rendering the body's content meant per-block CSS (e.g. `core/cover`'s own positioning/overlay rules) never made it into the page at all. Content now renders first (captured into a variable), then whatever got newly enqueued as a result is diffed and printed, alongside the base `wp-block-library` handle.
  - A "constrained" layout block's own per-instance CSS rule (blockGap spacing, alignfull child margins, etc.) is compiled by WordPress's Style Engine and normally flushed by `wp_enqueue_stored_styles()` — itself gated to only output when actually called from within `wp_footer` (block themes) or `wp_head` (classic themes). Now calling `wp_style_engine_get_stylesheet_from_context('block-supports')` directly — the real function that compiles that CSS, with no such gate — and printing its output ourselves.
  - The `--wp--style--global--content-size`/`wide-size` custom properties a "constrained" layout's max-width depends on (plus color/spacing preset variables, including this site's own `wgs-hero-spacing` fluid preset) come from `global-styles`, a stylesheet only ever registered by `wp_enqueue_global_styles()` — itself only hooked to `wp_enqueue_scripts`, which in turn is normally only fired from *inside* `wp_head()`. Now calling `wp_enqueue_global_styles()` directly so it registers regardless.
  - With no theme stylesheet loaded, nothing was resetting the browser's default `body` margin, pushing a full-viewport-height Cover block just past 100vh and causing an unwanted scrollbar. Added a minimal inline reset (`html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }`).
- `global-styles` and Astra's heading `text-transform: uppercase` are believed to be genuinely separate mechanisms — Astra's transform is expected to live in its own classic customizer-generated CSS, not in theme.json — so restoring `global-styles` should not reintroduce it; verifying this directly against prod is still pending as of this release.

## [2.5.2]
### Changed
- Tightened the Maintenance Page editor notice's wording, and replaced the parenthetical settings reference with a real clickable action button ("XO Functions Settings", via the notice's own `actions` option) linking straight to Settings → XO Functions → Maintenance Mode.

## [2.5.1]
### Fixed
- **2.5.0's Maintenance Page editor notice never actually appeared** — confirmed live on stage immediately after deploying: a plain `admin_notices` callback is not surfaced on the block editor screen the way it is on classic wp-admin screens, so nothing rendered at all. Replaced with the editor's own JS notices store (`wp.data.dispatch('core/notices').createNotice(...)`, via `enqueue_block_editor_assets` + `wp_add_inline_script()`) — the actually-supported mechanism for a persistent in-editor notice, the same one Yoast/Rank Math use for theirs.

## [2.5.0]
### Added
- **Edit-screen notice on the designated Maintenance Page**: David, 2026-08-29 — the block editor's own "Template" field keeps showing whatever template is assigned, which misrepresents what actually happens once Maintenance Mode renders that page directly (2.4.0+) and ignores it entirely; left as-is, that's confusing UX for anyone editing the page. Shows a notice on that specific page's edit screen only, worded differently depending on whether Maintenance Mode is currently on (Template has no effect right now) or off (still applies for now, until switched on). (Superseded same day by 2.5.1 — the notice mechanism used here didn't actually render.)

## [2.4.1]
### Fixed
- **Maintenance page's featured-image cover block rendered with no background image**, and its full-bleed layout was squished into a narrow centered box — both caught live on stage right after 2.4.0 shipped (David: incognito test of Wagner's Maintenance page, a full-bleed `core/cover` block with "use featured image" enabled). Two distinct causes:
  - Dropping `get_page_template()` in 2.4.0 also dropped the `$wp_query`/`setup_postdata()` call that used to point the *global* `$post` at the maintenance page. `core/cover`'s "use featured image" support is a server-rendered dynamic block that resolves its image via `has_post_thumbnail()`/`get_the_post_thumbnail_url()`, both of which default to reading `$GLOBALS['post']` — with no post context, it silently rendered with no image. Restored the same global-`$post`/`WP_Query` setup, just without going back to `get_page_template()` for the actual template.
  - `xo_render_maintenance_page_html()` was unconditionally wrapping every page's content in a fixed `max-width:640px` centered box with its own heading above it — appropriate for the no-page-configured fallback message, wrong for a real, designed page (this one was built full-bleed specifically so it wouldn't look like a bare error screen). That wrapper (and the redundant injected title) now applies only to the fallback case; a real page's content renders exactly as authored.
  - Also stopped re-running `the_content`'s own output through `wp_kses_post()` — that's for sanitizing raw, un-rendered post content, not for re-filtering already-rendered block HTML, and it risked silently stripping attributes (e.g. the cover block's own inline `min-height` style) that rendered blocks depend on.

## [2.4.0]
### Changed
- **Maintenance Mode now renders its own minimal, theme-independent HTML shell instead of the active theme's template hierarchy**: David, 2026-08-29 — Wagner's Golf Shop's Maintenance page rendered full header/nav/footer chrome on prod's Astra + Elementor site (matching whatever page template was assigned there), but no chrome at all on stage's ona-pro block theme (a "no title" template with no Astra equivalent). Since this is fleet-shared code, not built for one theme, `xo_maybe_serve_maintenance_page()` no longer calls `get_page_template()` — it now calls a new `xo_render_maintenance_page_html()`, which outputs a plain, self-contained `<!DOCTYPE html>` document (still calling `wp_head()`/`wp_footer()` for SEO/analytics/favicon plugin compatibility) with just the designated page's title and content, styled minimally by the plugin itself. Looks the same regardless of which theme a given site in the fleet runs, rather than depending on whatever page template happens to exist there.

## [2.3.2]
### Fixed
- **Fatal error in `extend/wp-frontend/wp-frontend.php`, live incident on Wagner's Golf Shop production, 2026-08-29**: `add_filter( 'widget_text', 'wp_do_shortcode', 11 )` and the equivalent `wp_nav_menu` filter referenced `wp_do_shortcode`, which is not a real WordPress function — core's actual function is `do_shortcode()`. This had sat dormant since `@since 1.3.2` because nothing had ever triggered the `widget_text`/`wp_nav_menu` filters on a site where this module was active. It surfaced the moment `xo-functions` was deployed to Wagner's `wagnersgolfshop-production` for the first time: prod had no prior `xo_functions_settings` option, so `xo_get_default_toggles()` defaulted every module (including `wp-frontend`) to "on" simultaneously, and prod's Astra + Elementor stack calls `apply_filters( 'widget_text', ... )` on nearly every page via Elementor's Text Editor widget — turning a dormant typo into a site-wide `Uncaught TypeError` on the live store. Root-caused directly from Kinsta's PHP error log (`logs/error.log`), not inferred. Immediate mitigation was disabling the plugin on prod (folder renamed, not deleted) to restore the site; this fixes the actual bug. Any other site that has never exercised these two filters could have the same latent bug — worth a quick check before assuming any site is unaffected just because it's never errored.

## [2.3.1]
### Changed
- **Maintenance Mode bypass is now role-based, not hardcoded to `manage_options`**: Wagner's Golf Shop has its own custom `website_manager` role (`users.php?role=website_manager`) that also needs the real site to keep working during a maintenance window, and other sites in the fleet have their own roles this plugin has no way to know about in advance (David, 2026-08-29). The settings tab now shows a checkbox per role that actually exists on the site, built from `get_editable_roles()` — the same function core's own Users screens use — instead of any fixed list. Administrator still always bypasses regardless of the saved selection, so misconfiguring the list can't lock an admin out of their own site.

## [2.3.0]
### Added
- **Maintenance Mode** (`extend/wp-core/maintenance-mode.php`, Settings → XO Functions → Maintenance Mode): pick an existing Page to serve as the site's maintenance page, the same way WordPress core's own Reading settings pick the Front Page / Privacy Policy Page (`wp_dropdown_pages()`), and the designated page gets a matching "Maintenance Page" label in the Pages list (`display_post_states`) — David, 2026-08-29, ahead of the Wagner's Golf Shop production relaunch. While enabled, visitors who can't `manage_options` get that page's own content (rendered through the active theme's normal template hierarchy, so header/footer/styling match the live site) with a `503`/`Retry-After` response instead of the real site; logged-in admins always see the real site. Deliberately its own per-site option storage (like Content Ordering), not the network-wide module-toggle option — which page to show, and whether a site is currently "down," aren't things one network-wide flag could represent across a fleet.

## [2.2.3]
### Changed
- Content Ordering source-filter checkbox state now persists per-user in the database (`xo_ordering_source_filters` user meta, saved via AJAX on every checkbox change) instead of the browser's `localStorage` — David, 2026-08-06: "it should save similar to the admin colors in my profile settings," since a preference tied to one browser resets on logout or in a different browser, which isn't how any other per-admin WP setting behaves.

## [2.2.2]
### Added
- **Content Ordering source filters**: each column now has a row of checkboxes (one per distinct source found in it — Core, each plugin, each theme) to show/hide items by source, since a site can easily have a couple dozen `show_ui` post types once every plugin's own internal types are counted. Unchecking a filter never touches the actual saved selection — if it would hide an item that's currently checked, its filter checkbox shows a "N selected hidden" badge so that's never silently invisible (David, 2026-08-06).
- Already-selected post types/taxonomies now sort to the top of each column's list, so the current configuration is visible at a glance without scrolling a potentially long list.
### Changed
- 10px left margin added to each row's checkbox for breathing room from the table edge.

## [2.2.1]
### Fixed
- **Taxonomy term ordering excluded every term without an order value yet** — turning ordering on for a taxonomy made its terms vanish from its own admin screen, and any post using an as-yet-unordered term showed no term at all (David, 2026-08-06, live-tested immediately after 2.2.0). Root cause, confirmed by reading `WP_Meta_Query::get_sql()`: 2.2.0's `'orderby' => 'meta_value_num', 'meta_key' => 'xo_term_order'` (via the `get_terms_args` filter) builds an implicit meta clause that defaults to an `INNER JOIN` against `wp_termmeta` — filtering out, not just sorting, any term lacking that meta key. Rewritten via the `terms_clauses` filter instead, with an explicit `LEFT JOIN` and a `COALESCE(...) ` fallback to alphabetical order for any term not yet touched by a drag — nothing is ever excluded.
### Changed
- **Settings consolidated into one page** (David: "keep all settings specific to XO consolidated," reachable "from a link on the plugins admin screen as well as a main item under Settings"): the Content Ordering screen is no longer its own Tools page — it's a tab on the same page as the existing Modules toggles, now under Settings (was Tools) with a "Settings" link added to the plugin's row on the Plugins list. Modules and Content Ordering can't literally share one page under multisite though (module toggles are network-wide, living in Network Admin; content ordering is per-site, living in each site's own admin — genuinely separate WordPress admin areas) — the page shows whichever tab(s) are relevant to the context it's opened from: both tabs on a non-multisite site, Content Ordering only on a multisite subsite, Modules only in Network Admin.
- **Content Ordering screen redesigned**: post types and taxonomies now list side by side in two columns instead of stacked, with larger column headings, and each row now shows a **Source** column (WordPress Core / Plugin: *Name* / Theme: *Name*) — determined by walking the call stack at the moment each post type/taxonomy registers (`registered_post_type`/`registered_taxonomy`), not a hardcoded lookup table, so it's accurate for any plugin/theme on any site. David: with every `show_ui` type on a site listed, it wasn't obvious at a glance which were core vs. a specific plugin.

## [2.2.0]
### Added
- **Content Ordering settings screen** (`extend/wp-core/ordering-settings.php`, Tools → Content Ordering): a site admin now picks which post types and taxonomies get drag-and-drop admin list-table reordering, per site — no code editing required. Replaces 2.1.9's `xo_orderable_post_types` filter, which only a developer could set and applied the same list fleet-wide regardless of what a given site actually runs (David, 2026-08-06: the utility needed to genuinely replace the "sort any post type"/"sort any taxonomy" plugins it was meant to retire, not stay scoped to the one CPT it was first built for). Deliberately its own settings page/storage, not folded into the existing "XO Functions" module-toggle screen — that screen's setting is network-wide under multisite (one shared list for the whole network), but which post types/taxonomies exist is inherently per-site; this new screen always saves with plain `get_option()`/`update_option()`, which are already blog-scoped even on a network.
- **Taxonomy term ordering** (`extend/wp-core/taxonomy-ordering.php`, new): terms have no native `menu_order`, so order is stored in a dedicated `xo_term_order` term meta key and applied via the `get_terms_args` filter — to every `get_terms()` call for an orderable taxonomy (front-end included, not just wp-admin), matching how the category-ordering plugins this replaces behave. A newly created term in an orderable taxonomy is given an explicit end-of-list order value on creation (`created_term`), so it doesn't unexpectedly sort to the front via a term-meta `LEFT JOIN`'s `NULL`/`0` before anyone's dragged it.
### Changed
- `extend/wp-core/post-type-ordering.php` generalized: `xo_get_orderable_post_types()` now reads the new settings-screen option instead of the `xo_orderable_post_types` filter (removed). A post type still doesn't need `'supports' => ['page-attributes']` for this to work — `menu_order` is a native column on every post regardless.

## [2.1.8]
### Added
- `extend/wp-core/search-url-slug.php`: redirects `?s=` search URLs to a clean `/search/{term}/` slug, with its own rewrite rule (self-flushed once via an option-flag guard, no manual Permalinks visit needed).
### Fixed
- The search URL redirect (previously pasted inline into `extend/wp-core/index.php`, sourced from a WPBeginner tutorial) had no matching rewrite rule at all, so every search 404'd after redirecting — the same bare snippet had been copy-pasted across several past one-off client projects (now archived in `.wip/`, replaced with pointer comments to this module) without ever being fixed. Adding the missing rewrite rule introduces a new failure mode if the redirect isn't scoped correctly (the clean URL itself also satisfies `is_search()`, so a naive check redirects it to itself in a loop) — fixed by keying the redirect specifically on `isset( $_GET['s'] )` rather than `is_search()` alone.
### Changed
- Renamed `wpb_change_search_url()` → `xo_redirect_search_url()`, matching this project's naming convention instead of the tutorial source's.
- `urlencode()` → `rawurlencode()` for the redirect target — this is a URL path segment, not a query string.

## [2.1.7]
### Changed
- No entry recorded prior to this file's split from ROADMAP.md — see plugin header `Version:` in
  `xo-functions.php` for the current released version; backfill this entry if you have the
  original notes.

## [2.1.3]
### Optimized
- Stripped out the redundant `XO_VERSION` global PHP constant.
### Fixed
- Resolved the WordPress 6.7+ `_load_textdomain_just_in_time` architectural warning by moving
  version data exclusively to the core DocBlock plugin header.

## [2.1.2]
### Added
- Infrastructure: initialized the automated Kinsta cloud deployment pipeline using local Git hook
  archives and SSH/SCP secure tunnels.
- Framework: injected dynamic `plugin-update-checker` (PUC) framework linking child endpoints to
  the MainWP template provisioning vault.

## [2.0.0]
### Changed
- Architectural shift: rebuilt the plugin with an isolated module loader loop checking saved
  configuration toggles before loading extended components.
</pre>
